subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-month-old infant is admitted with poor feeding, lethargy, and hepatomegaly. Echocardiography shows a dilated cardiomyopathy, and funduscopy shows pigmentary retinopathy. His mother's pregnancy was complicated by severe preeclampsia with elevated liver enzymes and low platelets, and his newborn sister died of a similar illness. Laboratory studies show glucose 38 mg/dL with low urine ketones and elevated hydroxyacylcarnitines (C16-OH).
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase is part of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, and its deficiency causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, pigmentary retinopathy, and peripheral neuropathy. Long-chain fatty acid metabolites from the affected fetus accumulate in the maternal circulation and are associated with maternal HELLP syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting but not cardiomyopathy, retinopathy, or maternal liver disease; acylcarnitines show C8 rather than hydroxy-C16.
explanation_incorrect.B: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II deficiency in infancy causes cardiomyopathy and hypoketotic hypoglycemia without retinopathy, and maternal HELLP is not a feature.
explanation_incorrect.C: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causes cardiomyopathy and hypoketotic hypoglycemia with elevated C14:1 acylcarnitine, but not pigmentary retinopathy or maternal HELLP.
explanation_incorrect.E: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I deficiency causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly with elevated free fatty acids, without cardiomyopathy or maternal disease.

educationalObjective: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causes infantile cardiomyopathy with retinopathy and is associated with maternal HELLP syndrome or acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
